The way to see this is as if the HTML parser algorithm had an additional boolean parameter, "created for the HTML fragment parsing algorithm", that is at times consulted to produce slightly different outcomes.

Hopefully at some point we'll adjust the HTML parser algorithm to make the parameters it has more visible and not as implicit as the setup is now.

@annevk Thanks for clarifying. But still you describe it in general (not specifically). Give at least one example that will describe: "**parser was originally created for the HTML fragment parsing algorithm**". 

I understand the creators of the specification more clearly knows the entities they describe in the specification. But readers can not always understand what the author conceived, describing this or that part of the specification. I ask you to show an example of at least one, so that the same person as I understood what the means **parser for the fragment** more specifically without abstractions.
The algorithm is used by https://w3c.github.io/DOM-Parsing/ to define `innerHTML`. Is that what you mean?

@annevk  I'm not sure what I mean about what you think.
But let me [quote](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#parsing-main-inforeign) the specification (It's one of many examples):
> - **A start tag whose tag name is one of: "b", "big", "blockquote", "body", "br", "center", "code", "dd", "div", "dl", "dt", "em", "embed", "h1", "h2", "h3", "h4", "h5", "h6", "head", "hr", "i", "img", "li", "listing", "menu", "meta", "nobr", "ol", "p", "pre", "ruby", "s", "small", "span", "strong", "strike", "sub", "sup", "table", "tt", "u", "ul", "var"**
> - **A start tag whose tag name is "font", if the token has any attributes named "color", "face", or "size"**
> 
> Parse error.
>
> If the parser was originally created for the HTML fragment parsing algorithm, then act as described in the "any other start tag" entry below. (fragment case)
> 
> Otherwise:
> 
> Pop an element from the stack of open elements, and then keep popping more elements from the stack of open elements until the current node is a MathML text integration point, an HTML integration point, or an element in the HTML namespace.
> 
> Then, reprocess the token.

Look at sentence until word _otherwise_. What should happen to this case (fragment case)? In the otherwise case, everything is simple. What an example of this fragment case, I honestly do not understand this moment.

```
<!DOCTYPE html>
<svg></svg>
<script>
document.querySelector("svg").innerHTML = "<b>"
</script>
```
It means that you process the "b" start tag per the "any other start tag" rules, which suggest to insert an element in the same namespace as the parent (SVG namespace) in the parent.

in the thread called:

> - A start tag whose tag name is one of: "b", "big", "blockquote", "body", "br", "center", "code", "dd", "div", "dl", "dt", "em", "embed", "h1", "h2", "h3", "h4", "h5", "h6", "head", "hr", "i", "img", "li", "listing", "menu", "meta", "nobr", "ol", "p", "pre", "ruby", "s", "small", "span", "strong", "strike", "sub", "sup", "table", "tt", "u", "ul", "var"

Where the item we are interested in is:
> If the parser was originally created for the HTML fragment parsing algorithm, then act as described in the "any other start tag" entry below. (fragment case)

You gave me a snippet of html code. I rummaged through the specs and came to the next chain of the algorithm. If I am not right somewhere, tell me.

So in order to get into: 
> If the parser was originally created for the HTML fragment parsing algorithm, then act as described in the "any other start tag" entry below. (fragment case)

We must first go here - https://w3c.github.io/DOM-Parsing/#extensions-to-the-element-interface which describes the algorithm for the work of innerHTML. From this algorithm we see that: 

`...fragment be the result of invoking the fragment parsing algorithm...`. 

Where we see another transition - https://w3c.github.io/DOM-Parsing/#parsing But this is not all if we look at the first paragraph of the algorithm we will be dropped here - https://www.w3.org/TR/html5/single-page.html#html-fragment-parsing-algorithm
And we get to do this paragraph completely to get the tree of elements. I correctly understand that the paragraph: **Parsing HTML fragments** - partially repeats the points of a regular parser for an html page? For example, here's what: 

> - **Any other element**
Leave the tokenizer in the data state.

It means that things from the html parser are used, right? That is, Parsing HTML fragments partially uses parser html points?
It turns out that when we execute the algorithm **Parsing HTML fragments** we will get there where I ask, that is in:
> If the parser was originally created for the HTML fragment parsing algorithm, then act as described in the "any other start tag" entry below. (fragment case)

Right?
I don't really understand what you're asking, but yes, the HTML fragment parser uses the HTML parser (and the HTML parser knows when it's invoked by the HTML fragment parser).

@annevk Perhaps due to the fact that I did not quite describe in detail you did not understand. But I will say this: the question was where did we get to the parsing fragment branch. This I briefly described. I wanted to understand whether I understand the algorithms correctly. Did I correctly described getting into the parsing fragment? But it’s still good that you answered on part of my question (Since the script is called by HTML parser, therefore HTML parser knows when the HTML fragment is called. Right?) And there was another question: _"Fragment parsing for foreign content is broken at the moment." - what do you mean?_ I correctly understand that you referred specifically to the problem that using parsing fragment does not create elements of a specific namespace? `xmlns` doesn't really have an effect in HTML documents. What I meant that it's broken for foreign content is explained in the issue I linked.

It does sound like you roughly understand how this works, but as I said, part of this is currently not correct (see aforementioned issue).
It's hard to tell if it's not detailed, but it seems roughly correct. And the standard is wrong.

@annevk And the last question. You mentioned that: _"HTML parser knows when it's invoked by the HTML fragment parser."_ HTML parser knows because it processes the <script> element. Which in turn calls the API (for example innerHTML) and this API calls the HTML fragment. Therefore - _"HTML parser knows when it's invoked by the HTML fragment parser"_. Right?
No, when `innerHTML` is invoked, the fragment parser gets invoked, which invokes the HTML parser. That another instance of the HTML parser might also be on some callstack is not relevant.
@annevk So it turns out that fragment parser calls HTML parser. And HTML parser knows when fragment parser is called just because fragment parser called him. Right?
Yes.
@annevk understanded! I have a request to add to the specification examples of use of fragment parser. Is it possible?
Yeah, more examples are generally always welcome.

I also think it would be correct to leave references to documents that use the mention `fragment parsing algorithm`.

As an **example** with `innerHTML` might look like this (you have a convention on how **example** blocks designed):
